name: Parquet
desc: A waxed parquet floor running away to the vanishing point where the laying pattern is the subject — because each block's grain runs a different way, the same drifting light reads bright on one block and dull on its neighbour at ninety degrees, so the whole floor shimmers in a zig-zag as the pools cross it, cathedral figure wanders through every block and traffic has dulled a lane down the middle; herringbone, mitred chevron, basketweave, a bordered Versailles panel, dark ebony, or a cyan setting-out plan.

energy.doc: how hard the light pools work the floor — anisotropic flip between blocks, wax specular, and the scroll rate

scale.doc: block size in world units — at min a fine mosaic parquet, at max colossal blocks

density.doc: how much dust turns in the light above the floor

speed.doc: how fast the floor streams toward the viewer

wear.doc: joint width, scuffing, and how dulled the traffic lane down the middle is

hue.doc: timber hue — from honey oak through to cool grey-washed

x.doc: vanishing point x as a canvas fraction

y.doc: horizon y as a canvas fraction — everything above it stays fully transparent so the bg shows through

style.doc: aesthetic: classic stepped herringbone / mitred chevron, the grain zig-zagging in continuous Vs / basketweave, pairs of blocks turned against each other / a bordered Versailles panel, diagonal weave inside a running frame / near-black ebony, the figure only just visible / a cyan setting-out plan — the laying pattern as pure line, no wood at all

seed.doc: timber lottery — per-block tone, figure and how the cut wanders
